A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Compact Hausdorff Space|compact Hausdorff space]] and $K \subseteq X$ [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed]].
Let $I_K = \set {f \in \map C X: f \restriction_K = 0}$.
Then:
:$\map C X / I_K \cong \map C K$
as [[Definition:Algebra over Ring|algebras]].

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a [[Definition:Ring Homomorphism|ring homomorphism]].
Then:
:$R / \map \ker \phi \cong \Img \phi$

object_map.reformulation: Realize C(K) as the image of restriction, so that the kernel-quotient pattern identifies it with a quotient of C(X).

validity_conditions: Surjectivity of restriction needs the Tietze extension theorem, hence normality of X.
K must be closed, so that it is a compact Hausdorff space and Tietze applies.
proof_plan:
Define $\rho: \map C X \to \map C K$ by $\map \rho f = f \restriction_K$.
$\rho$ preserves sums, products and scalar multiples, so is an algebra homomorphism.

A compact Hausdorff space is [[Definition:Normal Space|normal]].
By the [[Tietze Extension Theorem]], every $g \in \map C K$ extends to some $f \in \map C X$, so $\rho$ is [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]].
